scope: Second requested three-pass review of software/offline resource compatibility and publication preparation. No router execution or hosting changes.

rounds.focus: Common/capture and opkg/apk fixtures: accepted minimum, rejected older application, wrong-purpose rejection, tampering rejected before compatibility hints, catalog minimum enforcement
Publication retry identity and ZIP entry consistency; prior compatibility/storage-failure and publishing identity regressions

findings.problem: Renaming an unchanged archive keeps its content hash and reused a manifest with the old asset filename; uploading would use the new filename but public verification would request the old URL.
findings.fix: Reject retry when the archive filename differs from the existing verified signed manifest. Preserve the immutable original signed manifest.

findings.problem: Converting archive names to a set discarded duplicate entries; publishing preparation accepted ZIP files that the client rejects.
findings.fix: Reject duplicate entries and the same excessive entry count as the client before creating a signed preparation manifest.

rounds.focus: Actual Qt worker/service signals carry both application-update and bundle-update errors, clear stale offers, finish once and retain installed local status. Existing update and feedback-edge regressions.

limits: No Debian runtime, frozen executable rebuild or physical router installation performed.
Qt signal delivery checked synchronously through actual QObject signals; no new threaded event-loop or visual acceptance claim.
No online publishing, resource archive replacement, app restart, or platform-size audit changes.
No repeat of the entire previous 132-test suite: current production changes are confined to publication preparation and passed the relevant 23-test suite.
